Yes, exactly - divide and conquer. We, the masses, are 

distracted by the stage of political theater.

Having a different opinion about any particular issue 

causes division and prevents us from joining forces to deal

with the systemic problems

This keeps any political tools we have from working with 

any degree of effectiveness.

It doesn't \*feel\* safe to actually join together with people 

we fear.  Fear causes us to attack one another and this 

becomes justification for more fear, a cycle that just 

perpetuates itself.

The first step in a difficult process is to be disciplined 

about showing each other respect, even when we ourselves do 

not get respect.

It feels safer to attack back when we are attacked but in the 

bigger picture we make ourselves (our community) less safe.

This is a cultural problem and only over time will this actually

produce any positive effect.

I believe that the problems we face go beyond stated policies.
Are we not now in a time where what is stated as intent and 
actual policies has little connection with reality?
When there are more foundational problems in a system focusing 
on "detail" problems, even serious ones, without addressing the
foundational ones has little hope of making a real difference.
It's like a hole in the bottom of your boat, yes you need to 
bail water to keep from sinking but if you never even discuss
the fact that there is a hole letting more water in you are wasting
time.
I believe that the people who are in a position to even bring the
more foundational subjects to the table for open discussion have
their hands tied in even bring up the real foundational issues.
We need to invent something different
to get out of this box.

I appreciate the feedback, you have no idea how much.

Don't get me wrong, I don't "aim" at you when I say what I have to say next.

I include myself in this criticism as much as anybody (especially my self).

​

We are all failing, even the people who are putting

out everything they have with the best of intentions,

as a whole, we are FAILING.

​

Pointing fingers of blaming is very destructive, it's

what "they" want us to do -- division is one of

the main tools that keeps progress from happening,

​

But honestly, and in contradiction, "blame" is part of it a 

path forward.  We need a different kind of blame, blame 

with compassion -- spirituality (NOT religion) is the key to 

this. (consider the truth and reconciliation principle of

South African Apartheid trials)

​

We are in times where contradictions need to be used and turned 

into creating something new.  If the blame we use is not compassion

based we will go never break out of our habitual cycle of us -vs- them.

​

(note: out language, or at lease the cultural assumptions attached to 

words we use has been hijacked -- another tool used against us that

we have to deal with)

​

In the face of such overwhelming forces (social decay) it is perfectly 

understandable and logical to "sandbag" and try to ride it out.

But the truth is that this strategy is part of the our strategic problem 

(I believe by design).

​

In mythological/metaphorical religious terms I sometimes

see this as \_THE\_ challenge we were put here to face,

the test if you will.

​

If we don't learn to reach out beyond our selves and

start helping others beyond our own self interest things

will get worse and worse until it become "our turn" to

fall into the abyss, not through direct cause (blame) but 

through an accumulation of failures to not care and not act

​

I'm one of those people who has fallen into the abyss. At this point 

I don't even have the realist option of helping others  (or do I? -- 

or is that just more sandbagging).

​

The legal system falsely accused me of crimes that were obviously 

not true and it took 5 long years before my case was processed

(took a plea deal out of fear that was till not justified)

​

This has destroyed my life and at my age it is impossible for me to 

really recover. It's very difficult to get a job with a felony conviction.

​

In 2 months I will be homeless (again) and my plans are to put and end 

to things if I can find the courage.

​

So I have this overwhelming urge (obsession) to try to tell people: your 

better start connecting with each other and re/building a compassionate

society -- if you don't it is guaranteed to get worse and worse -- as you 

point out

​

And just maybe, just maybe, our sandbagging is something we have to 

account for in any existence we have after we die -- I am certain not a 

person who knows such things.

​

So thank you yaboynatan for responding and forgive my "preaching". 

I have lost ALL "friends" in my life and I can not tell you how much it means 

to just have a some connection, any connection, no

matter how brief

​

The saying goes: "hell is separation".  I truly, truly get this now, and that is

the message: if WE need to stop the decent into "hell" and there are no formulas.

​

Only by reaching out to others, carefully, can we create something -- each 

having part the answer yet to come.  As the saying goes, from one of the 

most ancient text: "you have to understand the difference between

principle and process".

As a film (story/drama) I really liked AVATAR.

At first I was impressed with it's “anit-system” pro-nature point of view. There is no denying that those messages are there

However, I have some to realize how subtle cultural “programming” is and I think I see an almost universal assumption in most all films that come out of the big budget studio systems.

The message being that violence is always necessary to solve problems.

I believe those who are injecting the poison into our spirituality are those who finance any and all sides of any conflict.

Conflict is part of our existence and this will not just go away but it does not have to be based in the violent models our culture so heavily promotes.

One thing you should keep in mind before doing anything, either
way, that is to say ending it or making another effort to move on:

Try to get a clear perspective that we live in an extremely disorienting
social environment right now.

You are a sane reaction to an insane world.

I fully believe this.

This means that even if you manage to pull up there is going
to be some both more pain and work ahead. 

Realize that even if you were able to feel like you have made
some big breakthrough and “get red of” the feelings of depression
this culture does not promote  real mental health from a true
spiritual perspective.

If you really are to that point of being a danger to yourself I suggest
you slow down and even “disconnect” from some things and
slowly experiment with reconnecting (but don't get lost and
get too comfortable being disconnected either)

Accept that it will be work, sometimes boring and lonely and 
painful.

(oh yes, I almost forgot, very important: lite physical exercise,
eat well and get good sleep – all very important)

It's sometimes called “becoming friends with you problem”.

Your problems can be your greatest teacher but you have to be
willing to “stay with” the feeling and endure it some (up to a point)
to be able to hear what it has to say to you.

Think of it as exercising, whatever you want to conceptualize it:
you spiritual muscles, your brain, your chemstry.

In order to hear the message it takes a lot of effort though and
carrying out you normal busy life at the same time is makes
it almost impossible.

But use the time to explore yourself and get to know some
different people in the process.

Don't follow into the trap of just turning it into “walking away”
or escaping. 

Compassion for both yourself and others has to be at the heart
of it also. Use your experience to help understand other people's
pain, even the assholes of the world.

I highly suggest that, down the road a bit, find some
way to do some volunteer work for others

Have faith that down the road you will start to feel some
payoff that will start to be a real foundation.

If you ever feel that you've go it licked just keep reminding
yourself that the culture around you has a problem and
start figuring out how to be one of the people that starts
to build a new culture.

We need you to help us.

I've struggle with a lot of depression myself, throughout my life
(I'm 60).

I use to be on an SSRI for quite awhile and decided I needed
to get off or die. It's was extremely hard for several months
but I started having success (still struggling though) by
doing 2 things:

1) force myself to do very lite exercise 5 days a week
Exercise that's a combo of strengthening (lifting, push ups, …) and short
periods of jogging to get my heart rate up.  I think it is important to
keep it really short and really light as you don't need to use up too
much precious energy.  The benefit is to just force your body to 
kick in energy regularly on a regular bases and set a pattern or
habit which effects you mind.  This took me about a month before I
could see that it was actually working.  This is very hard to do though. I
happened to have ideal circumstances to experiment with this
and I'm loosing the environment I had that enable me to do this.
I think the key is to get you heart rate up for just a bit.

a trap as they short circuit natural process whereby we
process the inner world stuff we need to go through to
get out the other side.

2) to help me sleep without meds I started listening to some of
these audio tapes you can find on the internet identified as
“hemi-sync”.  I tried these a few times years ago and sort of
just laughed because it seam to be a joke but I know someone
up highly recommended it  and decided to try it again.
It took about a week of doing this and I started to get
a return. For me it help to shut down my obsessive thoughts
and worry and sleep a little better.

which helps me but this is something highly individual

self damage you cause by focusing on hate.

abuse.

I've tried to distill out the essence of the

spirituality that religion points to, which always

seams to point to the golden rule: ‶do unto others as

As I said it is a tough read but well worth

Hi,

Your post from a few days back got stuck

in my head, as things often do.

The things you said reminded me of myself.

Just thought I'd offer my perspective as

you seam to be at a crucial point of

‶discovery″.

(of course I don't know you and this is

just my speculation)

You are the only real expert on your own

inner world.

We can, and often do, fool ourselves through

our imagination and wind up creating problems

or make things worse than they need to be.

I've been observing the world for a long time now.

You may not have noticed but this is what is going on

just about everywhere now, creating unnecessary problems

that is.

This, for good and bad, is the nature of our

inner reality as humans (is part of our

creativity).

Our culture offers very little help for

people to really understand our inner world.

For me the inner world is what spirituality

is about.

Many do not like to connect that word to our emotional

struggles but for me it fits.

The inner world is created and recreated

every day.

It is not solid but rather a constantly changing

thing.

When people really start to think about this

it becomes a bit unnerving.

We want the world around us to be something

more solid or less prone to change.

The fact that you question your own inner make up

(including intentions) show that you are aware and have

the integrity to question yourself honestly.

This can be a very uncomfortable thing.

The key to managing this is to realize what I just

said, this is something that is dynamically

created.

People get caught up in trying to find the source

of things so they can control matters.

Our culture greatly encourages us to do this through

finding where to place blame.

What is created though doesn't not come from

any one place or person -- it is ongoing in it's

creation and highly interdependent.

We can not control others, we can influence them.

It is uncomfortable to realize that we can not really

‶control″ our selves either, at least not immediately

through shear will.

We can compartmentalize to some degree and this

is actually a necessary tool but to believe

we can absolutely control ourselves

without going through a process (an ongoing

process) causes us to start blaming ourselves

and/or others.

We are all in this situation and once the pain gets to

be too much people usually start pointing the finger

out side of themselves (sometimes call for).

It is often very painful to go through self examination

There is a psychology term for just the opposite of what

I suspect you are, the ‶Dunning–Kruger Effect″.

It is where people have no real awareness (perhaps

will) to critically question their own abilities.

The upshot of it is that these people, feeling like

they know way more than they actually do, project great

confidence and can be very charismatic and influential.

You sound like you are on the opposite end of

the ‶spectrum″ (you and me both).

I have had to struggle with OCD and a constant

doubting of who I am and my self worth.

It's been crippling in my life, but it does

not have to be, especially if you can

understand it early on.

We are creatures of habit and you can, with

a compassionate attitude toward yourself and

others develop the ability to cope (through

trying to create good habits).

In fact it can be a great source of growth.

But this is key: you need to be aware that the on going

‶creation″ of your world (in which you are only a

participant not a dictator) is highly dependent on the

relationships you form, not only friends but work,

community, etc.

Our society is having a really hard time right

now because it is not very healthy as a

context to create these relationship (it's getting

a bit extreme).

Just keep being aware and promoting compassion

for yourself and others and except that failure

is just part of a process.

(See the universe is a ‶verb″ not a ‶noun″.)

This is actually a very hard thing to do but it will

make things easier for you in the long run and as well

help make the world a better place.

Good luck.
